title: Narrow Compatibility Hint Schema and Version-alias Requirements for Model Intake
creator: Aisha Tan
description: Clarify the minimal, machine-readable compatibility hint schema and version-aliasing rules that must be provided by all new open-model submissions into the catalog. This ticket narrows scope from the earlier broad intake PRD: we define a small deterministic manifest + runtime probe contract (compatibility hints) that the runtime and catalog UI can consume to make safe routing and pinning decisions without requiring full model execution at ingest time.
requirements: Provide a 1-page JSON manifest (model.manifest.json) attached to every intake bundle: fields: name, primary_variant, semantic_version, architecture_hint, tokenizer_spec, max_sequence_expected, affinity_tags

Compatibility hint fields: runtimes_compatible (list of runtime tokens), required_kv_cache_shape (optional), quantization_support (none/int8/fp16), known_incompatible_kernels (list), suggested_fallback_variant (optional)

Version aliasing: support a top-level aliases map so submitters can declare stable aliases (e.g., 'latest-stable' -> 'v1.2.3') and an immutable release id; alias resolution must be deterministic and recorded in the catalog entry

Minimal automated checks on ingest: tokenization sanity (same token count for canonical test prompts within +/-10%), manifest schema validation, signature verification for provenance if signed, and a lightweight runtime probe that runs a small zero-shot decode to verify API compatibility (<= 500ms on probe infra)
Runtime probe contract: probe must publish tags: {probe_latency_ms, probe_outcome: pass|warn|fail, profiling_signature} to the catalog ingestion log and must not contain user data
Catalog UI/console: surface 'compatibility confidence' score derived from manifest hints + probe results; allow engineers to see raw manifest and probe logs
Fallback mapping policy: when runtime in target region lacks exact kernel support, router may map to suggested_fallback_variant if manifest declares it and probe_outcome != fail
Backward compatibility: existing catalog entries without manifests should default to conservative routing (no auto-unpin), and a migration script should mark them as 'unknown-compat'
Security: manifest and aliases are part of the tamper-evident entry and must pass security review for any external weight submissions
Telemetry: record ingest-time metrics: manifest_schema_version, probe_latency_ms, probe_outcome, alias_resolution_time, and store as strings/tags for dashboards
tradeoffs: Performing a runtime probe at ingest gives stronger signals but increases ingest time and cost; chosen approach: keep probe lightweight (single short prompt) and optional for experimental channels
Requiring full runtime compatibility tests would be ideal for safety but is impractical for scale; instead we rely on compact profiler signatures + tokenization checks

Allowing submitters to declare suggested_fallback_variant reduces routing surprises but requires clear rules to avoid circular aliasing; we will ban cross-alias cycles and validate references on ingest
Tighter manifest schema reduces ambiguity but increases friction for submitters; we aim for minimal mandatory fields with optional extras for advanced models
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline accepts a model bundle with model.manifest.json and creates a catalog entry where aliases are resolved to immutable release ids
Automated manifest schema validator runs on ingest and blocks submission if mandatory fields are missing with clear error messages
Runtime probe executes for 95% of non-experimental submissions within the budgeted probe timeout and emits probe tags to the ingestion log
Console displays a compatibility confidence score and a link to raw manifest and probe logs for every new catalog entry
Router uses manifest.hints to allow fallback mapping to a declared suggested_fallback_variant when direct kernel support is not present and probe_outcome != fail
Migration script marks pre-manifest entries as 'unknown-compat' and adds a backlog item to request manifests for top 200 most-used models
Security review sign-off has been obtained for manifest format and aliasing rules for external weight submissions (security_review_required = true)
open_questions: Do we allow submitters to declare multiple aliases per release (e.g., 'latest' and 'latest-stable')? Proposed: yes, but aliases must be unique across catalog namespace
Should the runtime probe be mandatory for Dedicated and Private ingestion channels? Proposed: mandatory for Dedicated, optional for Free/Community channels
How do we monetarily budget probes for community contributions? Need an allocation policy for probe infra credits
What exact tokenizer test prompts should be used for tokenization sanity? Suggest set owned by catalog team and configurable per ecosystem
How to expose the 'compatibility confidence' score computational formula in the console while avoiding gaming by submitters?
